record.paper_title: Zero-Temperature Dynamics of Ising Spin Systems Following a Deep Quench: Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Homogeneous Ising dynamics in dimension at least three
record.original_question: Consider a zero-temperature stochastic Ising spin system with nearest-neighbor Hamiltonian H = −∑Jxy σxσy, initial spin configuration σ0 drawn from the symmetric Bernoulli product measure, and standard continuous-time single-spin-flip Glauber dynamics: energy-lowering flips are accepted, energy-increasing flips are rejected, and zero-energy flips are accepted with probability 1/2. For homogeneous ferromagnets or homogeneous antiferromagnets on Zd, or on any other lattice not already covered by the odd-number-of-neighbors type-F result, in dimension d ≥ 3, what is the dynamical outcome? Equivalently, is the system type I, meaning almost every site flips infinitely many times; type F, meaning almost every site flips only finitely many times; or type M, meaning both finitely flipping and infinitely flipping sites have strictly positive spatial density?

evidence.quote: Consider the stochastic process σ t = σ t(ω ) corresponding to the zero-temperature limit of Glauber dynamics for an Ising model with Hamiltonian, H = − ∑ Jx,y σxσy .
The initial spin configuration σ 0 is chosen from a symmetric Bernoulli product measure (denoted Pσ 0), corresponding physically to a deep quench.

The densities ρF and ρI depend only on d, µ, and possibly lattice type, and of course satisfy ρF + ρI = 1. We characterize the triplet ( d, µ , lattice type) as being type F or I or M (for mixed) according to whether ρF = 1 or ρI = 1 or 0 < ρ F , ρ I < 1.

For Ising spin systems with Hamiltonian (1), and J , σ 0 and ω chosen as discussed in Sec. 1, the problems of the dynamical outcomes of the following situations remain open: 1) Homogeneous ferromagnets (and antiferromagnets) on the lattice Zd (or others except where each site has an odd number of neighbors) for d ≥ 3. Numerical results [2] suggest that these should be type I for d = 3 and perhaps 4, but may possibly be type F (or M) for d ≥ 5.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d \ge 3$ and consider the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ (or any other infinite vertex-transitive lattice in which each site has an even number of nearest neighbors). Define the homogeneous nearest-neighbor Ising Hamiltonian
$$ H(\sigma) = -\sum_{\langle x,y\rangle} J\,\sigma_x\sigma_y, \qquad \sigma_x \in \{-1,+1\}, $$
with a fixed coupling constant $J \in \{+1,-1\}$ (ferromagnet or antiferromagnet). Let the initial spin configuration $\sigma^0 = (\sigma^0_x)_{x \in \mathbb{Z}^d}$ be chosen from the symmetric Bernoulli product measure (so each $\sigma^0_x$ is independently $\pm 1$ with probability $1/2$). Run continuous-time zero-temperature single-spin-flip Glauber dynamics: each site $x$ has an independent rate-$1$ Poisson clock, and when the clock at $x$ rings, the spin $\sigma_x$ is updated according to the local energy difference
$$ \Delta_x H = 2\sigma_x \sum_{y \sim x} J\,\sigma_y, $$
namely the proposed flip $\sigma_x \mapsto -\sigma_x$ is accepted with probability $1$ if $\Delta_x H < 0$, rejected if $\Delta_x H > 0$, and accepted with probability $1/2$ if $\Delta_x H = 0$.

For a site $x$, let $N_x(\omega)$ denote the total number of times $\sigma_x$ flips during $t \in [0,\infty)$. Define
$$ \rho_F = \mathbb{P}(N_0 < \infty), \qquad \rho_I = \mathbb{P}(N_0 = \infty), $$
so $\rho_F + \rho_I = 1$. The triple (dimension, coupling, lattice) is said to be:
- type F if $\rho_F = 1$ (almost every site flips only finitely many times),
- type I if $\rho_I = 1$ (almost every site flips infinitely many times),
- type M (mixed) if $0 < \rho_F < 1$ and $0 < \rho_I < 1$.

Determine, for the homogeneous ferromagnet (and homogeneous antiferromagnet) on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ (and on other regular lattices each of whose sites has an even number of neighbors), with $d \ge 3$, whether the system is of type I, type F, or type M.
artifact.status_search_result: The classification of homogeneous ferromagnetic/antiferromagnetic zero-temperature Glauber dynamics on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ for $d \ge 3$ (type I vs. F vs. M) remains open. Subsequent work has clarified related questions (e.g., biased Bernoulli initial conditions and $p_c(\mathbb{Z}^d)$, fixation on hexagonal lattice, behavior on hypercubes), but the symmetric Bernoulli case on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ in dimensions $\ge 3$ has not been resolved; numerical evidence suggests type I in $d=3$ (perhaps $d=4$) and possibly different behavior in higher $d$.

status_evidence.title: Zero-temperature Glauber dynamics on Z^d
status_evidence.snippet: Studies fixation in zero-temperature Glauber dynamics on Z^d with Bernoulli(p) initial conditions; discusses p_c open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work addresses related fixation questions but does not resolve the symmetric (p=1/2) classification on Z^d for d>=3.

status_evidence.title: Zero Temperature Dynamics of Ising Systems on Hypercubes (2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent paper studying zero-temperature Ising dynamics, indicating the broader area remains active.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues on type I/F/M classification problems, with the Z^d symmetric case still not settled.
